definitions.explanation: Describing something that follows the style, customs, or sensibility of an earlier era, whether positively (nostalgic, traditional) or negatively (outdated).

examples.japanese: {昔風|むかしふう}の{家|いえ}に{住|す}みたい。
examples.english: I want to live in an old-style house.

examples.japanese: この{喫茶店|きっさてん}は{昔風|むかしふう}の{雰囲気|ふんいき}がある。
examples.english: This café has an old-fashioned atmosphere.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{昔風|むかしふう}の{料理|りょうり}を{作|つく}るのが{上手|じょうず}だ。
examples.english: My grandmother is good at making old-fashioned cooking.

notes:
A compound of {昔|むかし} (the past, old times) and {風|ふう} (style, manner). Describes things that follow the style or customs of an earlier era. Can be either neutral/positive (nostalgic, traditional) or mildly negative (outdated) depending on context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {昔風|むかしふう}の{家|いえ}: old-style house
- {昔風|むかしふう}の{味|あじ}: old-fashioned flavor
- {昔風|むかしふう}の{考|かんが}え{方|かた}: old-fashioned way of thinking
- {昔風|むかしふう}の{暮|く}らし: old-style lifestyle

SIMILAR WORDS:
- レトロ: retro — loanword with a more positive, trendy nuance; emphasizes fashionable nostalgia
- {古風|こふう}: old-fashioned, archaic — more literary; can suggest elegance or quaintness
- {旧式|きゅうしき}: old-style, outdated — more negative; implies something is behind the times
- {昔|むかし}ながら: traditional, as in the old days — emphasizes continuity from the past to the present

cross_references.label: traditional, as in the old days
